messages:
ivy: Quick follow-up on pin/rollout schema: proposing a tiny, deterministic micro-pin token we can store in the hot KV (<=80 bytes) and keep a full human-readable manifest in object store for audits. Idea name: MPT1 (micro-pin token v1). Thoughts?

samir: Love the mem savings. Key question: what minimal fields to decode in the hot path vs what to leave in the manifest? Also how do we support partial rollouts without repinning?

leo: Hot path needs a few things only: model_fingerprint(20B), epoch_id(varint), rollout_bucket_id(small int), fallback_ptr(varint), expiry_ts(opt). Keep weights out of token, map rollout_bucket_id -> routing table in-memory. That allows retargeting without repinning.

ivy: Good, separate routing. Proposal for MPT1 layout: prefix "MPT1." + base64(payload) + "." + sig. Payload binary-packed: tenant_varint | model_fp(20B) | epoch_varint | rollout_bucket_varint | expiry(4B opt) | flags(1B) | key_id(2B). Sig = HMAC-SHA256(k, payload) truncated to 8 bytes. Typical token ~56-72 bytes.

ops-jan: Ops note: our hot index stores ~tens of millions rows, cutting per-value size would reduce RAM significantly. Migration must be additive. Plan: dual-write index value -> {"mpt":"MPT1...","manifest_url":"s3://...","manifest_hash":"sha256:..."}. New resolvers prefer mpt. Old clients keep using manifest_url.

sec-maya: Security: truncated HMAC is acceptable if we rotate keys and monitor weird patterns. Need an emergency revoke push so resolvers can get tiny denylists for hot retirements. Per-request blacklist is too heavy.

samir: How do resolvers behave on sig failure? fallback to manifest fetch and verify full manifest signature, emit metric token.verify_fail. Also increment token.fallback_rate. Gate flip on fallback_rate threshold.

leo: Caching: control-plane should cache token->expanded fields (short-lived) for traces and Console. Resolvers can include expanded hints in spans when available. Console expand API fetches manifest_url for human-readable details.

ivy: Edge-case: partial rollback targeted to a tenant subset. We'll publish tenant-scoped revoke messages via push channel keyed by tenant_id or token-hash. Resolver checks in-memory set before trusting token. That stays cheap.

ops-jan: Migration playbook draft: (1) start dual-write for 3w (2) enable mpt-first on canary resolvers (3) monitor token.fallback_rate, token.verify_fail_rate, p99 latency (4) if fallback_rate < 0.2% and no latency regressions, roll out to 25% -> 100% (5) keep manifests in object store for audits forever.

samir: Observability: add metrics token.verify_fail_rate{tenant,rollout_bucket}, token.fallback_rate, token.expiry_reject_count, token_age_hist. Also traces link token->manifest fetch id for Console.

sec-maya: Key rotation: use KMS-managed signing key. Token includes key_id. Resolvers pull verification keys by id and cache for short TTL (30s). On key mismatch they fallback to manifest fetch. Document rotation roll-forward carefully to avoid mass failures.

leo: Performance: ensure decode+verify path is <200us p99 on resolver. Also put a small LRU cache for token->decoded to avoid repeated HMAC ops. Cache size tuned per region; even 100k entries cuts CPU for hot tenants.

ivy: Long-term: support a chained micro-delta option later if tenants need rich audit diffs without big manifests. For now keep single-token + manifest model.

ops-jan: Ops additions: snapshot job to compact manifests for tenants that churn heavily; revoke push channel implementation; migration checklist doc. I'll draft playbook.

samir: Action items: @leo write resolver PR to parse MPT1 and verify truncated HMAC (ETA 1w); @sec-maya doc key rotation + revoke push (ETA 4d); @ops-jan migration playbook (ETA 3d); @ivy Console expand UX mock + trace linking (ETA 1w).

bot-snapshot: snapshot created: control-plane/rollout-proposals/mpt1/3999999999

ivy: Thanks everyone — we'll review PRs in the architecture sync next week. :thumbsup:
